Lukas — thanks for the forward. Draft bands below; I kept the math conservative and included ops notes. Happy to refine if you want different leverage assumptions.

Band A — Pay-as-you-go (no commit):
- Price: $10,000 / 1M tokens
- Rationale: handles burst but higher unit cost; baseline batching 20–30ms window, opportunistic prefix caching.
- Latency assumptions: with 150 TPS spikes, expect 99th ~420–480ms on shared capacity; recommend lightweight local retry logic and client-side concurrency shaping.

Band B — 12-mo commit (mixed reserved):
- Price tiers: $7,000 / 1M tokens (conservative deal), $6,200 / 1M tokens (if they commit to >20M/mo)
- Rationale: reserved pool + burst allowance for nightly batch; autoscale buffer for morning digest.
- Latency assumptions: 99th ~300–340ms at 150 TPS with suggested batching and KV caching.
- Ops notes: enable prefix/KV cache for repeated prompts; set batching to 10–20ms for user paths; quantify model to int8 where acceptable for non-critical paths.

Band C — Dedicated-heavy (reserved + private slots):
- Price: $4,800 / 1M tokens (volume + dedicated capacity)
- Rationale: predictable throughput and lowest $/1M; includes canary rollout for version pinning.
- Latency assumptions: 99th <280ms at 150 TPS with proper warmup and KV cache.

Example monthly invoices (using our customer combos):
- Conservative (19M tokens): Band B @ $7k => $133k/mo; Band C => $91.2k/mo
- Expected (21M tokens): Band B @ $7k => $147k/mo; Band C => $100.8k/mo
- Aggressive (23M tokens): Band B @ $6.2k (if >20M) => $142.6k/mo; Band C => $110.4k/mo
